notes:
Lead source: organic self-serve signup.
Context: early-stage CS SaaS (chat-first widget) — they embedded the Redwood hosted API to power agent assist + user-facing chat. Main issue: intermittent high latency causing the web UI to hit a 6s client timeout and drop the response. UX: some messages arrive delayed or the client shows an error and user retries -> duplicate requests.
Customer quote from perf call: "We see bursts where the chat just hangs for a couple seconds, then dumps an error — hard to explain to customers."
Current setup: using default endpoint in EU region due to initial account defaults; primary users are NA (West coast). Volume: low to moderate (peak ~20 concurrent sessions, ~10 reqs/s). Cost sensitivity: high — small monthly spend expected, want predictable costs.
Model preferences: prefer smaller cost-effective model for user-facing queries, reserve larger/expensive models for agent-assist reranks. Interested in Redwood suggestions for model variants + quantized options.
Immediate perf hypotheses from SE: region mismatch (EU -> NA users) + frontend short timeout + long prompt windows (they send full conversation history, ~1200 tokens). Also some cold-starts on rarely used model variant.
Advised quick wins given to customer: 1) switch to us-west endpoint for majority of users; 2) implement server-side request buffering + streaming so client doesn't hit 6s timeout; 3) trim prompt context: send only last 3 messages + condensed system prompt (~200-400 tokens); 4) set server request timeout 20s and client streaming keep-alive ping; 5) enable response caching for repeated FAQ queries; 6) add fallback to a cheaper model variant when latency > 700ms.
Security: asked about SOC2 and SSO — they require SOC2 Type II in contract and SAML SSO for console access. Asked about audit log retention and deletion windows.
Next steps (from AE/SE): create a short A/B test plan (us-east vs us-west) with scripted prompts and sampling window; ship a sample patch for trimming context; follow up with performance measurements (p50/p95/p99) and a recommended config for timeouts and streaming.
Open questions: whether frontend can handle streamed partial tokens; confirm data residency need (customer expects NA-only logs), final pricing approval timeline from finance.
Stitch to Jira: RDW-1198 created to track perf ticket and recommended config changes.
Notes tone: choppy, action-oriented; good candidate to convert if perf complaints resolved quickly.
